issues.title: C86-19 — High: the implementation worker cannot implement or fence files inside submodules
issues.cause: The rewritten prompt emitter still permits only root-worktree Git commands and finishes with a root git add and commit. The workflow's implement-finalize role still snapshots, validates, and diffs only the root occurrence. For a task owning vendor/src/x.ts, root Git cannot stage the contents inside vendor; a submodule-only commit leaves root HEAD unchanged and is rejected; manually advancing the root gitlink makes the fence see only vendor, not vendor/src/x.ts. The apparent end-to-end test manually commits inside the submodule through a callback that the generated worker contract does not provide and declares ownership of vendor rather than the actual nested file.

locations.role: Worker instructions allow only root-worktree Git commands.
Implementation commit and fence validation inspect only the root occurrence.
The deterministic finalizer diffs only the root checkout.
Fixture manually performs the forbidden submodule commit and masks nested ownership behind the root gitlink.

issues.provingTest: Prepare a task whose only owned path is a real file below a submodule. Have the fake worker follow the literal generated instructions, edit that file, and attempt the prescribed commit; the current workflow cannot return done. As a fence negative control, manually commit an unowned file inside the submodule and its root gitlink; a correct implementation reports the normalized nested path, while the current code reports only the gitlink.
suggestedFixApproach: Build an occurrence-aware ownership map. Snapshot, stage, commit, and diff owned paths in each occurrence deepest-first, then commit changed gitlinks in their parents.

Normalize every occurrence-local changed path back to its root-relative task path before fence comparison. Generate explicit git -C <occurrence-checkout> instructions for the worker instead of forbidding them.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: The manifest already supplies occurrence IDs, checkout paths, depths, and parent relationships for occurrence-aware ownership.
Merge already walks occurrences deepest-first and commits changed gitlinks in parents.

acceptanceCriteria: The literal worker contract can stage and commit an owned file below a submodule.
Implementation snapshots and diffs cover every owned occurrence and normalize local paths to root-relative task paths.
An unowned nested edit is reported as the nested path, and focused nested-worktree tests pass.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('implement commits and fences a file owned below a submodule', async () => { /* assert vendor/src/x.ts */ })

issues.title: C86-20 — High: a partial deepest-first merge is misclassified as a zero-progress lap
issues.cause: mergeTaskDeepestFirst may successfully move a source submodule and then fail its parent. The workflow returns the task as failed, recordStageOutcome increments mergedThisLap only for a completely merged task, and shouldEndQueue returns stuck when that count is zero. The spec intentionally keeps earlier source-layer merges, so the retry would not run against the same source state; stopping loses a potentially recoverable task.

locations.role: A child source layer can merge before a later parent layer fails.
A partially completed deepest-first walk is returned as a failed task.
The rewritten workflow forwards the failed merge result without recording source-layer progress.
Queue progress counts only fully merged tasks and declares the partial lap stuck.

issues.provingTest: Use a nested fixture in which the child source merge succeeds and the parent merge fails. Consume the real workflow envelope, prove the child source branch moved, and assert that the current queue has mergedThisLap equal to zero and reports stuck. The corrected queue must begin another lap, subject to the normal lap ceiling, because source progress occurred.
suggestedFixApproach: Track source-layer progress separately from fully merged task count, for example sourceProgressThisLap.
Set it when a failed merge result has a completed layer with status merged, reset it in beginNextLap, and apply the zero-progress exit only when neither a task nor any source layer moved.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: mergeTaskDeepestFirst already retains completedLayers when a later parent layer fails.
The queue already tracks per-lap full-task progress, carryover, and the lap ceiling.

acceptanceCriteria: A failed merge envelope records whether any source layer merged during the attempt.
The queue is stuck only when neither a task nor a source layer moved and failures remain.
beginNextLap resets source progress, and a child-merged/parent-failed regression begins another lap under the existing ceiling.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
return { stage: 'merge', status, completedLayers, parentResult }
// completedLayers retains child layers that moved before the parent failed.

issues.title: C86-21 — High: unexpected rebase/merge exceptions reject the workflow instead of entering the retry queue
issues.cause: The rewrite moved Git and filesystem operations into emitter roles but did not make their failure contract total. A failed merge emitter is retried and eventually becomes the generic merge-driver-no-result envelope, losing the concrete operational reason. A failed rebase-walk or parent-rebase emitter returns no agent result and the workflow explicitly throws, so that stage still rejects with no status/lastFailure envelope for consumeTaskWorkflowResult. The task can therefore remain unqueued and unreported, contrary to tasks 149 and 153.

locations.role: Missing emitter results throw from rebase or degrade to a generic merge failure.
Emitter roles execute throwing rebase, merge, close, ref, and cleanup operations.

issues.provingTest: Make the rebase-walk emitter exit nonzero after a deterministic Git or ref failure and have the workflow agent return no result, as it does when the command produces no valid result instructions. The current workflow retries and then throws instead of returning a blocked envelope. Separately create a leaf ref named refs/taskTools/merge-intents so merge persistence creation fails; the merge path returns only a generic driver-no-result reason. The fixed results must carry the concrete operational reason through queue carryover and reporting. A nested variant should merge the child first and trigger the failure only in the parent, retaining C86-20 progress data.
suggestedFixApproach: Make the rebase and merge primitives total and return typed failure reports, or wrap every stage-level primitive call in try/catch.

Normalize operational exceptions to a nonempty stage-specific lastFailure while preserving completedLayers, source-progress information, conflict paths, and merged-but-not-closed semantics once the root merge has landed.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: concreteMergeStageFailure already converts structured merge failures into nonempty actionable reasons.
Queue consumption already retains ordinary blocked and merged-but-not-closed failures.

acceptanceCriteria: Every rebase-walk, parent-rebase, and merge operational exception becomes a typed workflow result.
lastFailure keeps the concrete operational reason and preserves completed layers, conflicts, source progress, and merged-but-not-closed state.
Queue reporting accepts all normalized failure shapes, including child progress followed by parent failure.

remainingMinimalExample.code: if (!layerWalk) return { stage: 'rebase-test', task: N, status: 'blocked', lastFailure: 'rebase-walk driver returned no result' }

issues.title: C86-22 — High: missingFiles from the third/final plan review is ignored
issues.cause: runPlan performs the first verification, decrements reviewRounds, and handles rejected output only while reviewRounds is greater than zero. It makes three verifier calls but processes only the first two rejections. A third response containing missingFiles exits the loop and implementation begins with the old file fence and unrepaired plan. Task 136 requires widening and replanning whenever verification returns nonempty missingFiles and defines no final-round exception.

locations.role: The loop exits before processing the third verifier rejection.

issues.provingTest: Script verifier responses as rejected with ordinary fixes, rejected with ordinary fixes, then rejected with missingFiles containing b.ts. Assert that the authoritative task record, run-arguments snapshot, rewritten plan and brief, and implementer prompt all include b.ts. They currently do not.
suggestedFixApproach: Model each of the three rounds as verify followed by processing that result.

On a rejected third review, still widen and replan or apply feedback, but do not invoke a fourth verifier. Preserve the final verifier notes and verdict for the user gate so the unverified final repair remains visible.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: widenFilesAndReplan already persists missing files, refreshes the in-memory fence, and replans before another review.
The authoritative widening mutation is already locked and updates the run-arguments snapshot.

acceptanceCriteria: Each of the three review rounds is modeled as verify followed by processing that verifier result.
A final-round missingFiles rejection widens authoritative task state and repairs the plan without invoking a fourth verifier.
Final verifier notes and verdict remain visible to the approval gate when the repaired plan is not reviewed again.
The final implementer prompt, brief, plan, and ownership fence all include files introduced by the third review.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('third rejected review still widens and repairs without a fourth verification', async () => { /* assert b.ts reaches task state, brief, plan, and worker */ })

issues.title: C86-23 — High: accepted proposed tasks bypass the task-state lock and can race with close
issues.cause: The gate can invoke create-task while tail workflows are concurrently merging and closing. The generated create-task brief directs its agent to append to tasks.json directly. closeTasks holds the shared lock and publishes a whole-file replacement, but an editor that ignores that lock can overwrite the close or be overwritten by it, resurrecting a closed task or losing the new task.

locations.role: Accepted proposals may invoke create-task while tail workflows are active.
The skill tells an agent to edit tasks.json directly without the task-state mutex.
Close uses a locked whole-file replacement that can race with the unlocked editor.

issues.provingTest: In two real processes, make the append process read tasks.json and pause. Let closeTasks acquire the lock, archive and remove task A, and publish. Resume the stale append of task B and prove A is resurrected. Add the reverse ordering and prove B can be lost under the current direct-editor protocol.
suggestedFixApproach: Add a programmatic task-append command that resolves the authoritative project root, acquires withTaskStateLock, rereads current state, allocates the number, appends, and atomically publishes.
Make the create-task skill gather fields but call that command; it must never write tasks.json directly. Test both orderings with real processes and an acknowledged inside-lock barrier.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: withTaskStateLock and writeJsonAtomically are the established transaction boundary for task-state writers.
Close already rereads and publishes task state while holding that mutex.

acceptanceCriteria: create-task calls one programmatic append operation and never directly edits tasks.json.
Append resolves authoritative state, locks, rereads, allocates, and atomically publishes inside one transaction.
Deterministic real-process tests cover append-first and close-first without resurrection or loss.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
const pair = resolveTaskFiles(projectRoot)
return withTaskStateLock(pair.tasksPath, () => closeTasksLocked(taskNumbers, closureNote, pair, commitHashes))

remainingMinimalExample.code: Send the task draft to appendTask on quoted-heredoc stdin; never edit tasks.json directly.

issues.title: C86-24 — Medium: the shared six-workflow ceiling can be exceeded by the serial tail
issues.cause: Initial plan/implement launches maintain a six-entry sliding window. When one completes, the instructions refill the freed slot. Approval independently enqueues tail work, and the queue launch path checks only whether another tail is outstanding, not total outstandingEntries size. A valid interleaving is six planners, one completion, a replacement planner, then an approved task's rebase-test: seven workflows. Tests inspect the sliding-window and tail text separately but never model their shared capacity.

locations.role: Plan refill and tail launch use separate capacity decisions.
Tests inspect each instruction separately and miss the combined interleaving.

issues.provingTest: Drive an executable scheduler through six plan launches, one completion, one plan refill, then approval and rebase launch. Record every launch and completion. The current instructions permit seven simultaneous workflows. The corrected scheduler must never exceed TASKS_PER_COMMAND while still enqueueing approvals immediately and preserving one-at-a-time tail execution.
suggestedFixApproach: Put all launches behind one capacity-aware action selector. nextQueueAction, or its caller's executable state, should receive total outstanding count and return wait when it equals the cap.
Define whether a ready tail or a new plan receives the freed slot and test both plan-completion and tail-completion interleavings.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: nextQueueAction is already the executable selector for serial tail launch, wait, lap rollover, and reporting.
The emitted instructions already track outstandingEntries across plan/implement and tail workflows.

acceptanceCriteria: One capacity decision covers every plan/implement, rebase-test, and merge launch.
No enqueue/completion interleaving exceeds maxConcurrency, while tail execution remains serial.
Executable tests cover plan-completion and tail-completion slot allocation and approvals remain immediately enqueueable.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
const step = nextQueueStep(queue)
if (step) return outstanding.tail ? { kind: 'wait' } : { kind: 'launch', step }

remainingMinimalExample.code:
export type OutstandingWorkflowState = { any: boolean; tail: boolean; total: number; capacity: number }
if (step && (outstanding.tail || outstanding.total >= outstanding.capacity)) return { kind: 'wait' }
test('shared plan and tail launches never exceed capacity', () => { /* six plans, completion/refill, approval */ })

issues.title: C86-25 — High: an implementer can report done with a notes-only commit or without implementation notes
issues.cause: A done result is rejected only when root HEAD did not change. The later diff exempts the expected notes path from fence violations but never requires that path or any owned implementation path. A notes-only commit passes as complete, and an owned-file commit with no required implementation-notes file also passes. Existing coverage tests only the zero-commit lie.

locations.role: Completion validates only a changed root HEAD and never requires both notes and owned implementation changes.
The emitter finalizer reports only root HEAD and changed paths; it does not verify required artifacts.
Coverage checks only a worker that makes no commit.

issues.provingTest: Add two workflow-level cases: a worker commits only plans/task-N-implementation-notes.md, and a worker commits an owned source file but omits the notes file. Both currently return done; both must return blocked with distinct actionable reasons.
suggestedFixApproach: For status done, require the expected notes path in changedPaths and at least one task-owned path in the commit range.
Verify that the notes path is exactly preparedTask.notesFile and is present in HEAD, not merely untracked. Return a typed blocked result before approval if either requirement fails.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: Implement already snapshots HEAD, blocks a zero-commit done result, and computes ownership violations.
The worker contract already names the exact notes path and restricts staging to owned files plus that path.

acceptanceCriteria: Done requires the exact committed implementation-notes file and at least one committed task-owned implementation path.
Notes-only and owned-change-without-notes results are blocked with distinct actionable reasons.
Existing zero-commit and ownership-fence behavior remains intact, with workflow-level coverage for all three cases.

remainingMinimalExample.code:
test('done rejects notes-only commits', async () => { ... })
test('done rejects owned commits without notes', async () => { ... })

issues.title: C86-26 — High: emitter roles reload stale ownership from the private worktree and undo widening
issues.cause: The emitter's loadPreparedTask resolves and reads tasks.json under WORKTREE. Widening correctly updates authoritative state under SOURCE_ROOT and briefly writes a widened worktree brief, but the next plan or verify role calls loadPreparedTask again, reloads the stale private task record, overwrites the widened brief, and emits the old ownership list. The workflow's in-memory preparedTask.files update is not passed to the emitter. A separately launched implement stage has the same stale-fence defect.

locations.role: Every role reloads and rewrites task context from the stale worktree task file.
The workflow updates ownership only in memory, while subsequent emitter calls reload their own stale copy.
Widening correctly updates authoritative source state rather than the private checkout.

issues.provingTest: Prepare a task owning a.ts. Drive a rejected verifier response with missingFiles containing b.ts. Assert that widen-files updates authoritative tasks.json, then capture the immediately following replanner and verifier prompts: both must include b.ts and the regenerated brief must retain it. The current plan role reloads the private a.ts-only record and overwrites the widened brief. Also launch a fresh implement stage and assert that its prompt and returned fence include b.ts; current behavior reloads only a.ts.
suggestedFixApproach: Load the current task record using resolveTaskFiles(SOURCE_ROOT), while continuing to place the task brief, plan, notes, Git operations, and edits under WORKTREE.
Represent authoritative task-state root and task checkout root as separate fields so later code cannot accidentally use one for the other.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: Widening already resolves task files from SOURCE_ROOT and atomically updates authoritative tasks.json plus the run snapshot.
Worktree-local brief, plan, notes, Git, and edit paths are already rooted under WORKTREE and should remain there.

acceptanceCriteria: Every emitter role reads the current task record from authoritative SOURCE_ROOT task state.
Brief, plan, notes, Git operations, and source edits remain rooted in the private WORKTREE.
A widen-files result survives the immediately following replan, verify, and separately launched implement roles.
Types distinguish taskStateRoot from checkoutRoot so the roots cannot be accidentally interchanged.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('widened ownership survives replanning, verification, and a fresh implement stage', async () => { /* assert b.ts in every emitted prompt and fence */ })

issues.existingOpenTask: Task 87 is related to stale relaunch briefs but targets the superseded plan workflow and does not cover standalone implement ownership; no exact open item exists.

issues.title: C86-27 — High: post-approval rebase fence violations are discarded before merge
issues.cause: Rebase conflict and fix agents can edit and commit other occurrence layers, and those paths are collected as fenceViolations. A green rebase result may include those violations. consumeTaskWorkflowResult ignores tail-stage fence violations, while the generated orchestrator is forbidden to inspect results[] itself. The task can therefore merge changes outside its approved fence after the approval gate.

locations.role: Rebase records cross-layer changes and may return them with a green result.
Tail result consumption discards fenceViolations.
The orchestrator is forbidden to inspect the raw results array, leaving no alternate consumer.

issues.provingTest: Feed a real green rebase-test envelope containing a cross-occurrence violation into consumeTaskWorkflowResult. The current queue advances the task directly to merge and loses the exact occurrence and path. The corrected result must stop before merge and surface the scope change for an explicit re-gate.
suggestedFixApproach: Add persistent post-approval violation state to the queue and result adapter. A green rebase with violations should produce a requires-regate action instead of a merge step.
Display normalized occurrence and path details at the gate and require a new approval to advance. A retry alone is insufficient because the committed cross-layer edit remains in branch history.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: Rebase conflict/fix bookkeeping already records cross-occurrence touched paths as fenceViolations.
The plan+implement adapter already exposes pre-approval implementation violations in its normalized approval view.

acceptanceCriteria: Tail-stage fence violations survive result consumption and persist in queue state.
A green rebase with violations requires a new explicit gate and cannot advance directly to merge.
Tests cover clean green, violated green, rejected regate, and approved regate paths.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
for (const touched of advanced.touchedPaths) fenceViolations.push(touched)
return { stage: 'rebase-test', task: N, status: 'green', fenceViolations, sourceBranch }

remainingMinimalExample.code: Handle requires-regate with AskUserQuestion; enqueue merge only after explicit approval.

issues.title: C86-28 — Medium: failed final worktree cleanup is silently treated as a clean merge
issues.cause: After close, the workflow deletes merge persistence refs before attempting worktree and branch cleanup. A cleanup failure returns inherited status merged plus cleanupWarning. consumeTaskWorkflowResult treats it as unconditional success and drops the warning, and buildMergeReport has no cleanup-incomplete section. The existing locked-worktree test positively asserts an empty final report, enshrining silent residue.

locations.role: Persistence is deleted before final cleanup and cleanup failure retains merged status.
Queue consumption and reporting have no cleanup-incomplete state.
Test observes cleanup residue but expects the final report to be empty.

issues.provingTest: Force root worktree or branch deletion to fail after a successful merge and close. Consume the real envelope and build the report. The current report is empty although task artifacts remain and recovery refs are gone. The corrected report must name the residue; after unlocking, an idempotent retry must remove all refs and worktrees and clear the warning.
suggestedFixApproach: Retain merge persistence until worktree and branch cleanup succeeds.
Carry a cleanupIncomplete record through the workflow envelope, queue, and final report, including task number, warning, and retained artifact paths.
Provide an idempotent cleanup-only retry that deletes persistence last.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: MergedNotClosedTask and buildMergeReport already preserve merges whose archival step failed.
The merge role already separates merge, close, persistence, and final cleanup and returns cleanupWarning.

acceptanceCriteria: Merge persistence remains until worktree and branch cleanup succeeds.
Cleanup failure creates a reported cleanupIncomplete record with warning and retained artifact paths.
An idempotent cleanup-only retry deletes persistence last, and the locked-worktree test expects a nonempty report.

resolvedBoundaryExample.code:
export type MergedNotClosedTask = { taskNumber: number; commitHash: string; lastFailure: string }
return { unmerged: [...ceilingFailures, ...queueExitFailures], mergedNotClosed: queue.mergedNotClosed }

remainingMinimalExample.code:
try { removeTaskWorktreeAndBranches(...); deleteAllTaskMergePersistence(...) }
catch (error) { printResult({ ...report, status: 'cleanup-incomplete', cleanupWarning, retainedArtifacts }) }

issues.title: C86-29 — Medium: two live invocations of the same task can share and reset one clean worktree
issues.cause: createWorktreeForGroup treats a clean worktree whose HEAD equals or precedes source as reusable, then force-resets its task branch. It has no live-run ownership marker. Two sessions that prepare task N before either workflow writes its brief both receive the same directory and branch. The existing test codifies immediate clean reuse instead of simultaneous ownership.

locations.role: Clean Git state is treated as proof that the worktree has no live owner.
Test endorses immediate clean reuse and does not model concurrent sessions.

issues.provingTest: Start two real prepare processes for the same task behind a barrier. Exactly one should acquire ownership and the other should fail without resetting or modifying the first run's checkout. Both currently can succeed if they enter before either produces retained work.
suggestedFixApproach: Acquire an exclusive per-task owner lease atomically during preparation and release it only during final successful cleanup.

Include run or session identity and define an explicit stale-lease recovery operation that first verifies and preserves retained work. Clean Git state alone must not imply that no live process owns the worktree.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: worktreeHoldsRetainedWork already prevents automatic reuse from destroying commits or dirty edits left for recovery.
The task-state mutex demonstrates the repository's existing atomic exclusive-create lease primitive and fail-safe timeout behavior.

acceptanceCriteria: Preparation atomically acquires an exclusive per-task live-run lease before resetting or creating the worktree.
A concurrent preparation for the same task fails without resetting, modifying, or sharing the first run's checkout.
The lease records run/session identity and is released only after successful final cleanup.
Stale-lease recovery is explicit and preserves retained work; real-process tests deterministically prove single ownership.

remainingMinimalExample.code: test('two live prepare processes cannot acquire the same task worktree', async () => { /* first acknowledges lease; second fails without reset */ })

issues.existingOpenTask: Exact match: open task 104 requests a live ownership signal and rejection of concurrent same-task sessions.

issues.title: C86-30 — Medium: preparation writes task briefs into the canonical source checkout and never cleans them
issues.cause: The CLI writes every selected brief under the source checkout before creating task worktrees, and buildWorkflowArguments publishes canonical brief and plan paths. The workflow independently regenerates the brief inside the worktree and cleanup removes only the worktree copy. This produces visible untracked plans/brief-*.md residue after tackle-tasks runs.

locations.role: Preparation publishes canonical artifact paths and writes the brief into source.
Runtime creates and removes only the task-worktree copy.
Production-shaped success test does not assert source artifact absence.

issues.provingTest: Run the real preparation CLI and a successful task lifecycle. Assert that neither plans/brief-N.md nor a generated empty plan exists in the canonical source checkout before, during, or after the workflow, and that the files exist only in the task worktree when needed. Adding the source-absence assertion to the current production-shaped test fails.
suggestedFixApproach: Remove the source writeTaskBriefFile loop.

Create each worktree first, generate its brief there or let loadPreparedTask do so, and publish that worktree's absolute briefFile and planFile paths in group arguments instead of paths under repoRoot.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: Runtime task loading already creates the brief under WORKTREE and merge cleanup removes the worktree-local plan and brief.
buildWorkflowArguments already creates the task worktree before returning each prepared group.

acceptanceCriteria: Preparation never writes brief-N.md or an empty plan into the canonical source checkout.
Workflow arguments publish absolute brief and plan paths under the task's private worktree.
Transient artifacts exist only in the worktree when needed and are removed by successful cleanup.
Production-shaped lifecycle tests assert source artifact absence before, during, and after the workflow.

remainingMinimalExample.code: assert.equal(existsSync(join(sourceRoot, 'plans', `brief-${taskNumber}.md`)), false)

issues.existingOpenTask: Exact match: open task 105 requires transient plan and brief artifacts to stay in task worktrees and be absent from source.

issues.title: C86-35 — High: the rewrite no longer verifies that a planned result wrote the expected plan file
issues.cause: The pre-rewrite guard checked both that the planner returned the exact expected path and that the file existed. The import-free rewrite retained only the string comparison. No emitter role checks filesystem existence after the planner returns. A planner can report status planned with the expected path without writing it, and the workflow proceeds to verifier and implementer agents. The existing regression covers only an existing plan at the wrong ambient path, so it cannot detect the missing expected file.

locations.role: Plan validation compares the returned path but performs no delegated existence check.
Emitter roles include task-info and prompts but no plan-file existence/status role.
Regression covers a wrong existing path, not the expected path being absent.

issues.provingTest: Have the planner return status planned and planFile equal to the exact expected worktree path without creating the file. Make the verifier stand-in approve without reading it. The current workflow proceeds through verification and implementation instead of returning needs-clarification. Assert that neither verifier nor implementer is called after the corrected guard rejects the result.
suggestedFixApproach: Add a read-only emitter role such as plan-file-status that receives no arbitrary path, derives the expected plan path from task number and WORKTREE, and returns {exists:boolean}.

After every initial or replanned planned result passes the exact-path comparison, invoke that role and convert a missing file to needs-clarification before verification. Add both the missing-expected-path test and the existing wrong-path negative test.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: rejectPlannedWithoutExpectedPlanFile already rejects a planner-reported path that is not the exact prepared worktree plan path.
Emitter roles are the established boundary for delegated read-only filesystem checks because the workflow itself remains import-free.

acceptanceCriteria: A planned result is accepted only when it reports the exact expected path and that file exists in the task worktree.
The existence role derives the expected path from WORKTREE and N and accepts no arbitrary caller-supplied path.
A missing expected plan returns needs-clarification before verifier or implementer agents run.
Both missing-expected-path and wrong-existing-path regressions pass while the workflow remains import-free.
issues.existingOpenTask: No matching open task. This is a regression of the previously fixed task-worktree plan guard.

issues.title: C86-36 — High: retryAgent re-executes mutating emitter roles after their side effects have already landed
issues.cause: The rewrite routes deterministic mutations through agent calls and wraps every call in retryAgent. retryAgent cannot distinguish a command that failed before mutation from an agent that successfully ran the command but was killed or returned null before relaying its structured result. It therefore executes the same mutation again. The merge role can merge, close the task, delete persistence, and remove the worktree on its first attempt; a lost agent result then reruns against a deleted worktree and finally reports the task blocked even though it was already merged and closed. advance-conflict can similarly continue a rebase once and then retry against a no-longer-active rebase. Tests immediately parse and return emitter output, so none model result loss after command completion.

locations.role: The common retry wrapper is applied to mutating conflict, rebase, and merge driver roles.
These roles commit, continue or abort rebases, merge, close, delete refs, and remove worktrees before printing their result.
Harness always converts successful emitter stdout directly into the agent result and cannot simulate a lost result after mutation.

issues.provingTest: Drive a real merge-stage fixture with an agent wrapper that executes the merge emitter command on attempt one but discards its stdout and returns null. Let retryAgent launch attempt two. The current first attempt merges and closes the task; later attempts fail because cleanup removed the worktree, and the workflow reports blocked or no result despite completed state. Add the analogous advance-conflict case where the first command successfully continues the rebase but its agent result is lost.
suggestedFixApproach: Do not blindly retry a mutating role. Give each mutation an idempotency key and persist its typed result atomically before printing it, or split mutation from result retrieval so retries call a read-only receipt/status role.

For merge, record a run/task/stage receipt before returning and have repeated invocations return that receipt without re-running merge, close, or cleanup. For conflict continuation, persist or derive a reconciled state that distinguishes already-continued from never-started.

Extend the harness so the real emitter command can complete while the enclosing agent returns null. Assert that retry obtains the original receipt, performs no second mutation, and reports the actual final state.

resolvedBoundaryReference.role: retryAgent correctly retries missing results for read-only prompt and status roles and preserves valid falsy results.
Mutating roles are already centralized behind named emitter dispatch points, which provides a place to add idempotency keys and durable receipts.

acceptanceCriteria: Mutating emitter roles are never blindly executed a second time after their first attempt may have committed side effects.
Each mutation has an idempotency key and persists its typed result before returning output, or retries use a read-only receipt/status role.
A lost merge result is recovered as the original merged/closed outcome without a second merge, close, persistence deletion, or cleanup attempt.
A lost advance-conflict result is reconciled without continuing or aborting the rebase twice, while ordinary read-only retries retain current behavior.
